content: Validate CLI numeric flags with a digits-only regex before Number(), which otherwise accepts floats, hex, exponents, and coerces empty strings to 0. parseNonNegInt in scripts/kb.ts is the single validator for --days, --since, and --limit.

FTS5 bm25 ranks by term rarity, not by how many query tokens match, and clamps IDF so it never truly ties on common terms. Ranking tests must hold document length equal between compared rows and probe against the full fixture, since document frequency is a property of the whole table.

Before dispatching an implementer, touch and remove a probe file in each story directory using absolute paths; a sandbox can return EPERM on a directory that lists as writable. The failure otherwise surfaces later as a git ref error that reads like a bad branch name.

MUST-CHECK: this repo is public and git history is permanent, so anything ported from a private workspace is scrubbed in the same commit: org and repo names, CI filenames, issue ids and team prefixes, absolute paths. Leak tests and KB entries describe the shape of an identifier and never quote a real one, even in a comment, because the scan covers the test file and the KB too.
expect(a.version).toBe(b.version) across two files is vacuously true when both keys are absent. Assert a positive shape such as a semver regex on one side first.

MUST-CHECK: array-form spawn rules out shell injection but not endpoint injection; a repo or id carrying .. or extra slashes redirects a REST path. Validate the shape at the CLI boundary and again inside the pure function.

jq's length is defined on every JSON type, so a scalar satisfies a digits-only count guard and the following X[] iterates zero times with exit 0. Assert (X|type) == "array" before trusting a count, and reconcile the loop's iterations against it afterward.

MUST-CHECK: a path taken from agent-writable state (a run-state file, a cached payload) and handed to git -C is a code-execution sink, because a hostile .git/config runs commands on an ordinary read. The trust root is the operator-authored config, re-read fresh in the same fence; the mutable copy must agree with it and is never used in its place.

Tickets, specs, KB entries, and comments anchor code by file and symbol, never by line number, and never cite a line number of the file being edited. Prose is plain and short: one idea per sentence, said once, cut if it does not change what the implementer does.
The repo has no eslint or biome config and no lint script. "Typecheck and lint clean" here means bunx tsc --noEmit only.

Everything under plugins/drawbar/ is a git symlink into the root tree except .codex-plugin/plugin.json, which is a real duplicate guarded by a byte-parity test. Editing the root file edits the plugin, so there is no mirror step and a parity test between the two paths can never fail.

Before specifying copy, mirror, or parity work, check whether the destination is a symlink with git ls-files -s or readlink. diff follows symlinks, so identical output proves nothing, and a parity test written on that premise can never fail.
Asserting a usage string names -h with toContain("-h") passes vacuously because --help contains that substring. Match on a token boundary.

MUST-CHECK: never use git stash, git checkout <file>, or git restore <file> to reach a pre-change state while uncommitted work is in the tree; each discards that work silently. Read the old version with git show HEAD:<path> or a throwaway worktree, and undo a scripted mutation from a copy you made first.
MUST-CHECK: re-adding a key does not erase the old text; it moves to knowledge.archive.jsonl, which is gitignored but still on disk. A redaction must check the archive as well as the active file.
The owner-slash-repo leak rule scans every line of the ship runbook and the story-lead, so a new word/word pair such as lead/implementer trips it. Reword rather than widen the allowlist.

MUST-CHECK: a path-segment validator that blocks slashes and .. still admits newlines and other control characters, which are a path vector and a prompt-injection vector when the value reaches agent-facing prose. Reject [\x00-\x1f\x7f] at the shared string primitive so every field built on it is covered.

MUST-CHECK: git resolves a bare name through refs/tags before refs/heads, so a same-named tag can answer a later query about a different object even after refs/heads/<x> was verified. Pass the fully qualified refs/heads/<x> to every git call that reasons about the ref.

MUST-CHECK: each bash fence in a runbook is a separate process, so a later fence re-derives every variable it consumes from the source of truth and asserts each is non-empty; otherwise an ambient REPO or BRANCH from the operator's shell is trusted silently. A value a later step needs must be echoed to stdout, since a command substitution never leaves its fence.

Before removing a hardcoded environment anchor, ask what it gates: it may be the only thing keeping an unfixed vulnerability unreachable, so replace it with a fail-closed placeholder and fix the vulnerability first. Quote placeholders in shipped shell, or an unquoted <placeholder> becomes a redirection and assigns an empty string.

A plain {} flag bag lets --__proto__ reach Object.prototype and evade an Object.keys allowlist, and a plain lookup table answers to constructor. Build flag bags with Object.create(null) and guard table lookups with hasOwnProperty.

Write shell guards as `condition || { echo msg; exit 1; }`, never `! condition && { ...; exit 1; }`, so the success path leaves the exit status at 0. Avoid mapfile in shipped fences because macOS ships bash 3.2.
In shell, [ "$var" != "0" ] is true for an empty string, so a failed upstream read passes as success. Require a positive numeric match and print a distinct could-not-read message.

git rev-parse --verify --quiet and git merge-base --is-ancestor exit 1 for a genuine miss and 128 for a broken repository or bad object. Route the two to different reasons, or a moved checkout reads as a missing branch.

An injected git or gh runner takes an explicit validated directory and wraps spawn in try/catch returning a fail-closed result. Without those it runs in whatever directory the caller is in, and a missing binary throws a stack trace the bash caller cannot tell from slowness.

Tests built on injected runners prove nothing about the real tool's argv semantics or output format, because the fake was written by the same author. Drive the CLI once through a throwaway real fixture before trusting a retry or classification regex.

A staleness threshold or timestamp that is zero, NaN, or unparseable fails in both directions: too small compares fresh as stale, NaN never compares stale at all. Validate at the parse boundary and again inside the pure verdict, and route bad input to its own named refusal rather than either normal branch.

A green test with one well-formed degraded fixture can coexist with a guard that is unreachable in production. Before review, hand-probe empty, zero, NaN, unparseable, and future-dated inputs against the real module and ask which direction each one fails.

A dispatch guard is only real if the claim is durable before the action fires: build the claim, call the injected persist writer, then act. Test the ordering with a shared call log, including the case where the action throws.

A try/catch added in a fix pass absorbs the failure mode of every upstream guard whose test asserts only an exit code, so deleting those guards leaves the suite green. Assert the specific message each guard emits, and re-run the mutation set after a fix pass, not only before.

scripts/kb.ts validates every command from one COMMANDS table carrying typed flags, positional arity, and requiresStore; usage is derived from it, and help plus all validation run before resolveContext and ensureDir. An unknown flag, a value-typed flag without a value, and a boolean flag given a value all exit 1, and archive and compact refuse a missing store without creating it.

The installed plugin's cache is keyed by the manifest version, so a change ships only after bumping package.json, both .codex-plugin/plugin.json files, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the test in scripts/plugin.test.ts whose name pins the literal. Until then a run against the stale build passes while exercising none of the new code.

This repo declares no devDependencies, so bunx tsc --noEmit fails on bun-types until you install it, and in the sandbox bun add needs TMPDIR and BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR pointed at a writable scratch directory. Restore package.json from a copy afterward and delete the lockfile.

A .gitignore pattern containing a slash is anchored to the .gitignore's directory, so .drawbar/ship.config.json ignores only the root copy. Use a leading **/ to match at any depth and verify with git check-ignore -v against a nested path.

git ls-files -s reports the index, not the working tree, and mode 120000 only proves an entry is a symlink, not that it resolves. A symlink test also checks existsSync on the path, and a mutation of the tree must be staged before it can turn the test red.

A test asserting only the post-state of a destructive operation passes vacuously if the seed never landed, whether the cause is a wrong filename or an unset variable. Assert the pre-state count, and include one unseeded case for anything that can arrive empty.

A scripted mutation that fails to match leaves an unmutated tree that passes, which looks exactly like a surviving mutant; confirm the mutation landed before concluding anything. When reproducing a reviewer's mutation, apply it verbatim and check which test failed, because a kill by an unrelated test is not a kill.

A guard applied at several sites needs a test at each; mutating one site says nothing about the others. Enumerate the occurrences with grep and mutate each independently, especially fix-pass code, which is the least reviewed.

Mutation testing breaks code and watches a test fail, so a test that asserts repository or environment state reads as all survivors. For those, break the state it describes, such as replacing the symlink or editing the manifest, and confirm red.

A fixture of length two cannot distinguish first from last or i-1 from 0, so mutants swapping those indexes survive. Use three or more entries and assert the result is not equal to the wrong position's value.
A test runner's -t filter is a regex, so a title containing parentheses or brackets silently matches zero tests and reports 0 fail. Any harness that filters must assert a non-zero test count ran.

A proof that the suite passes with a tool absent from PATH is invalid if the scrubbed PATH also hides bun; the run dies with command not found and reads as a pass. Build the scrub directory under bash with IFS=:, assert the linked-binary count is non-zero, and assert bun resolves inside it.

Prove a regression guard red against the actual historical input that caused the defect, pinned as a fixture from a fixed commit, not a reconstruction. Never resolve that history through a moving ref like HEAD inside the test, which the fix commit itself will advance.
A test for a de-hardcoded value is blind to re-hardcoding if every fixture sets the variable to the old constant. Use a different value and assert both the match and the refusal.

When spawning an extracted bash fragment: read stdout and stderr together since echo goes to stdout, omit a key from Bun.spawn's env to test it unset since env replaces the child's environment, and re-wrap a loop body in its own loop so break behaves. Each of these has misreported a correct guard as broken.

A test that slices a fence out of a doc at a literal marker must first assert the marker occurs exactly once; a comment repeating the marker truncates the extracted script early, and a short script exits 0. Describe a command in prose inside comments rather than repeating its literal text.

When review findings, or a first mutation sweep, concentrate in one artifact or one clause while its neighbors stay clean, that piece is its own story, not a fix-pass item. A rule that must gather evidence from external tools cannot be held in prose and will keep accumulating findings until it is code.

A recalled MUST-CHECK left out of the brief instructs the violation, because the implementer builds what the brief says. Run a second recall shaped like the sink (git -C, trust root, path from state) rather than the feature, and let reviewers recall independently.

Before deleting a module, grep every surviving module for imports from it, and re-read each condition that only gated a call to it: a precondition left above an assignment becomes a verdict. A section still named for a guarantee it no longer enforces is the tell.

A rule whose clauses have different outcomes, such as three that clear a gate and one that means re-pick, must not sit under one header; an agent resolves the ambiguity toward proceeding. Mark the odd clause in place and give any retry clause a terminating condition.
